sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate faithfully encodes the complete conditional applicability conjunction, uses the supplied canonical ship-owned terms with correct datatypes and units, preserves conditional separation evidence without unconditional existence, and detects missing, malformed, or below-threshold separation measurements without allowing a compliant measurement to mask an invalid represented value. Deterministic validation is valid.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Reject the conditional check because FILTER NOT EXISTS passes when any one of multiple separation values is compliant, even if another value is below 0.76 m, and the separation property has no SHACL quantity structure. Constrain nltl:oilFuelTankOuterShellSeparation to the supplied ship-owned qudt:QuantityValue with exactly one value, decimal qudt:numericValue, and unit:M; retain the conditional violation query so an applicable ship with no separation value fails, and ensure the query cannot pass on a merely partial or malformed separation measurement.

Preserve the prior repair instruction and additionally correct the SPARQL unit mismatch: nltl:individualOilFuelTankCapacity is declared and constrained in unit:M3, but the query currently requires unit:M, so the applicability branch is wrong. Do not impose sh:minCount 1 on nltl:oilFuelTankOuterShellSeparation unconditionally, because the requirement is conditional and inapplicable ships may lack that measurement; retain the conditional violation check instead. Ensure the violation query detects a missing or below-threshold separation for an applicable ship without passing merely because another separation value is compliant, and align its separation structure with the exact ship-owned QuantityValue constraint (decimal numericValue and unit:M).

Deterministic validation prevents acceptance. Fix: Unknown canonical benchmark IRI(s): https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#individualOilFuelCapacity
Semantic validator feedback: Preserve the prior repair instructions. Replace the unknown nltl:individualOilFuelCapacity IRI in the SPARQL with the supplied canonical nltl:individualOilFuelTankCapacity; this genuinely misspelled/unknown term requires vocabulary matching. Use unit:M3 for that individual-capacity quantity, not unit:M. The applicability query must faithfully implement the complete conjunction: Category A or B, constructionDate >= xsd:date('2017-01-01'), aggregateOilFuelCapacity < 600 m3, and individualOilFuelTankCapacity > 30 m3. Retain the ship-owned QuantityValue structures for all three quantity properties, with decimal qudt:numericValue and the declared units. Keep oilFuelTankOuterShellSeparation conditional rather than imposing unconditional sh:minCount, but make the violation test fail when no valid separation measurement exists or when any represented separation is below 0.76 m; do not let one compliant value mask another below-threshold value. Remove the malformed/partial-value pass logic and use a deterministic violation formulation compatible with the exact SHACL structure. The candidate currently fails deterministic validation because of the unknown canonical property and does not faithfully encode the required individual-capacity applicability operand.

The candidate faithfully encodes the complete conditional applicability conjunction, uses the supplied canonical ship-owned terms with correct datatypes and units, preserves conditional separation evidence without unconditional existence, and detects missing, malformed, or below-threshold separation measurements without allowing a compliant measurement to mask an invalid represented value. Deterministic validation is valid.
